races.name: Heineken Low & No Bar Ebf Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Bacha
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd and 5th on good ground, so handles the surface shift reasonably, but is a genuine hold-up horse operating in a field with too many closers — will be further forward than ideal and the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations accordingly; Fahey stable in decent form.|

runners_data.name: Perryston
runners_data.note: Finished a tailed-off 10th on good at Goodwood on debut and carries a notable fade-in-finish flag; soft ground at Hamilton asks further questions of her stamina and Kevin Ryan's 3/35 over 14 days gives limited support for an immediate bounce-back.|

runners_data.name: Stay On Tab
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures of 63676 show limited ability, and her sole soft-ground run produced a 6th; a natural hold-up runner who will be pushed closer to midfield than suits her, and the headgear change has not yet delivered a breakthrough.|

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Two fourth-and-fifth finishes on good ground give a baseline of modest ability; Tim Easterby's 6/78 14-day strike rate is solid context, and she races fresh off 9 days, but her hold-up style in a race where pace is not expected to be searching makes a closing finish harder to execute.|

runners_data.name: Dadawada
runners_data.note: Shaped encouragingly for a prominent racer with a 4th on soft and a 5th on good, giving her the most relevant going experience in the field; headgear flagged as hood, which she has worn before, and Kellett's low 0/4 yard form over 14 days is the one caution.|

runners_data.name: Royal Strike
runners_data.note: Burke's yard has fired in 9 winners from 46 runners over 14 days — the standout trainer angle in this race; Royal Strike's form of 4th and 3rd has been over 6f on good ground, so the drop to 5f on soft is a query, but prominent-style runners with this training momentum must be respected.|

runners_data.name: Sneakin Pete
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no recorded form or last-run data and an UNKNOWN going profile; the wildcard of the race — James Sullivan takes the ride for a small yard on 2/9 over 14 days, so expectations should be measured.|

runners_data.name: Sod Hall Lane
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field, who shaped with promise when runner-up over this exact course and distance on good ground; the step up in ground conditions to soft is the primary unknown, but the ability to control her own destiny from the front is the key tactical asset in this race.|

races.paceDynamic: Sod Hall Lane is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine speed challenger to pressure her, she should slot onto the lead uncontested from the outset and control a measured, sustainable gallop on soft ground over five furlongs at Hamilton. Dadawada and Royal Strike will push forward to track her in the prominent positions, creating a conventional lead-group setup but not a searching early pace. The hold-up contingent — Bacha, Classyfied, Stay On Tab, and Perryston — will be held up behind, but the field contains more hold-up types than the map can genuinely accommodate at the rear, with Bacha and Stay On Tab most likely displaced into midfield rather than securing a true back-of-the-field position. Soft ground at Hamilton, which plays to stamina and those able to sustain their gallop, combined with an uncontested lead, firmly favours the front-running and prominent-racing profile in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sod Hall Lane Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sod Hall Lane secures the lead unchallenged and sets a soft but honest tempo that the hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: Sod Hall Lane dictates from the front on ground she handles, conserving enough energy to find again in the final furlong while those chasing from deep are left with too much ground to make up on soft turf; Dadawada and Royal Strike, tracking closely throughout, are best placed to challenge if she ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominents Swamp Late Trier
scenarios.trigger: If Sod Hall Lane goes too steady in front and the tracking prominent horses pounce decisively inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A very slow early gallop encourages Royal Strike and Dadawada to close sharply from just off the pace, with one of them getting a run and passing a tiring leader inside the final furlong; this shape suits horses that travel comfortably in the first two positions without necessarily leading.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a true end-to-end test on soft ground.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop from Sod Hall Lane burns off the prominent horses and leaves a gap for a hold-up runner to close from midfield in the final furlong; Bacha, with the highest OR in the field and a hold-up style, is best positioned to benefit if conditions truly stack against the front-runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At The Break
scenarios.trigger: If there is a significant incident at the start — a slow break, a stumble, or traffic problems — that reshuffles running positions fundamentally.
scenarios.body: Sneakin Pete, with no recorded form and completely unknown going profile, or an unexposed runner who finds daylight, benefits most from a scrambled scenario where tactical positions become irrelevant; soft ground amplifies the cost of losing momentum for hold-up horses trying to make late ground.

watchPoints.text: Sod Hall Lane sets the tempo completely unchallenged — if she controls the early fractions on soft ground, she may simply never be caught by a hold-up-heavy field that cannot bridge the gap.

Royal Strike carries the strongest trainer angle (K.R. Burke, 9/46 over 14 days) and races from a prominent position — watch for her making a sustained challenge inside the final furlong if the early pace is not truly severe.

Bacha and Stay On Tab are genuine hold-up types physically displaced into midfield by race shape — if neither can get back to their natural position, their probability of influencing the finish is materially reduced.

Dadawada's hood and soft-ground form (4th) make her the most interesting of the prominent-tracking pair — watch to see if she travels fluently behind Sod Hall Lane, as that travelling quality will determine whether she can mount a real late challenge.
Sneakin Pete is entirely unknown — watch the market moves and the paddock; if this runner shows any early speed at the break it could alter the pace shape significantly.

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Edgewater Drive
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a strong win record on soft going (four wins in soft/similar conditions from 15 runs), returning from 298 days off which is the key unknown — Wilf Storey has just one runner in the past 14 days suggesting a quiet yard, but the horse's course and soft-ground form makes it a natural beneficiary if fit.
runners_data.comment: Edgewater Drive was only eighth last time out but has a win two starts back, and a third three starts back suggests some consistency, but he has not raced in 298 days and the return from a lengthy absence is the clear concern for a gelding carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5-year-old has one soft-ground win at 6f and profiles as a prominent racer who will want to sit just behind Iris Dancer; low trainer strike rate over 14 days (0/16) is a slight dampener but the horse arrives in reasonable recent form with a handicap win at this trip on soft in the past season.
runners_data.comment: Lumenbourg won four starts back but has since finished fourth, sixth, and fifth in his last three outings, suggesting current form is modest; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 41 days off and 135 lb to carry make further improvement hard to bank on.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; Tristan Davidson in cracking recent form (4/10 over 14 days) and Rowan Scott takes the ride on an 8-year-old who has won on soft and over this C&D trip — blinkers applied and lightly raced for the yard, she is the key pace asset and sets the tactical shape for the entire race.
runners_data.comment: Iris Dancer arrives on the back of a fifth last time out and has a win in her last six starts, that victory coming five starts back, though a ninth two starts back and an unplaced run three starts back are harder to ignore; experience over today's trip and going offers some comfort at 134 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Camera Shy
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose form is over 7f on Tapeta rather than soft turf 6f, making the trip and going combination unproven; Connor Beasley is a competent booking but this horse's sole win came over 7f and there is no soft-ground evidence in the recent history to inspire confidence at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Camera Shy won five starts back but has finished no better than fourth in his last four outings since, suggesting he needs to rediscover that form; he has run over today's trip before and returns after a 27-day break carrying 132 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse that the redistribution model places into midfield given the glut of closers; his soft-going record shows one placed run from three attempts and without access to a true back-running position his chance is structurally compromised in this shape regardless of form.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and again four starts back, Big Apple Jack arrives in good order on a 14-day turnaround and has run over today's trip, though he remains winless in his last six starts and our rating ranks him ninth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: Won on soft at 6f at Catterick and is a natural hold-up performer who will be squeezed into a midfield role rather than coming from off the back — the style mismatch is real, but the soft-going win in the recent record (7th outing ago) gives her an outside profile claim if the race falls apart up front.
runners_data.comment: White Umbrella won two starts back but has otherwise struggled, finishing seventh on her latest outing and posting a largely modest recent profile — ranked well down on our figures here, she faces a stiff task despite having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 6-year-old is a prominent racer with a deeply underwhelming recent record — six, six, six, four, eight, eight across his last six — and no wins or places on soft going; maps to a reasonable position behind the leader but form figures give little encouragement on any ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with three consecutive eighths and sixths doing little to inspire confidence, Mount Ruapehu is hard to fancy from stall eight carrying 126 lb, ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie runner who is a hold-up horse in natural style, slotting into the midfield grouping by necessity; has won on soft previously and has recent course exposure, but the five-furlong wins on soft don't necessarily translate to six furlongs and the redistribution away from his favoured back-running slot hurts his cause.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Doon The Glen makes a compelling case hard to construct, with four finishes no better than fifth in his last five starts, though he does bring distance and going experience and a win in his last six to show he can find the line first.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for the same Jim Goldie yard pushed into the midfield pack; all form in the last five runs comes on good or faster ground, raising a genuine going concern on today's soft surface, and the horse has failed to win from 13 soft-ground appearances — both factors stack against a big showing.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with consecutive sixths before a return to third last time out, Summerstorms Dream faces a stiff ask from stall 12 carrying 116 lb, and a rating of 41 ranked bottom of this field leaves her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5-year-old is a hold-up type with no wins in soft-going conditions from four attempts; David Allan takes the ride and the horse's recent form string of 643972 offers little encouragement, though the proximity to the winner on a couple of occasions at 6f on good suggests ability if conditions were to suit.
runners_data.comment: Valentine Catcher shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, he has run over today's distance and going before, and our rating puts him clear of his official mark — the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, suggesting the winning thread remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Lesley's Boy
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey runner with a heavy soft-going run lurking in the form (16th at Haydock on soft) which is a significant red flag; the visor headgear is worn and the 4-year-old has form on Tapeta but soft turf form figures are deeply concerning — Oisin Orr cannot change the going profile.
runners_data.comment: Lesley's Boy brings experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 67 ranks him second among thirteen rivals, suggesting he holds strong claims here; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts, with consecutive eighths latest, and must prove he can recapture the third he registered five starts back.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4-year-old has failed to win in 12 soft-ground appearances and has a form string reading -99695 with the minus sign suggesting a non-completion; a string of ninth-placed finishes on good and soft at 6f makes this one of the more exposed runners in the field, and the going is not clearly in its favour.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Men Of Honour nevertheless holds a clear edge on our ratings over his 12 rivals, and having run over today's trip before, he arrives fit on just 11 days' rest carrying 130 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's 9-year-old is a natural hold-up performer with 10 runs on soft ground producing one win and two places — the experience on the surface is notable — but the redistribution into midfield means he cannot deliver his hold-up style, and at nine years old on a testing surface the race comes quickly enough for a horse whose last win at 6f on soft was some time ago.
runners_data.comment: Impressor arrives here fit on a 12-day turnaround, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and a speed rating of 68 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 57 implies; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and his latest efforts have been disappointing.

races.paceDynamic: Iris Dancer is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pressing rival for the lead — Edgewater Drive and Lumenbourg will look to track prominently but neither has the profile to force a pace battle on soft ground over 6f at Hamilton. With Iris Dancer able to bowl along at a controlled, self-set tempo, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically suits the leader and those racing just off the pace on this tight Hamilton track. The soft ground will stretch the field out early and penalise horses who are forced wide or unable to get competitive positions, compressing the effective tactical options for this field. This race shape strongly favours the lead-and-prominent profile — Iris Dancer dictating and Edgewater Drive or Lumenbourg travelling just behind represent the most advantaged positions. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear in a 13-runner field; Impressor, Big Apple Jack, White Umbrella, Doon The Glen and Summerstorms Dream are all genuine hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves racing in an unnatural midfield position rather than off the back, further reducing their ability to produce a meaningful late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iris Dancer Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer settles into an uncontested lead and the soft ground produces a steady, honest pace that the field cannot lift.
scenarios.body: Iris Dancer dictates every yard at a rhythm that suits her, with the soft Hamilton 6f failing to generate the strong gallop that true hold-up horses need to peg her back; the mare has course form, soft-going form, and a competent Rowan Scott booking.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Edgewater Drive or Lumenbourg track Iris Dancer closely and overpower her in the final furlong as the leader ties up on soft ground.
scenarios.body: The soft surface saps stamina from the front-runner in the closing stages and the prominent chasers, having been shielded by Iris Dancer's early pace, finish strongly past a tiring leader; Edgewater Drive's win record on soft and Lumenbourg's 6f soft win make both credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Iris Dancer is genuinely strong enough on soft ground to gut the field and allow a well-positioned midfield type to pick through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: A true pace collapse drags the race back to horses who have been settled in the first half of the field without burning energy early; Camera Shy and Valentine Catcher, hold-up types with soft-going credentials, are best placed of those not in the front rank if this scenario develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Run
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a genuinely strong pace with the field spread wide, allowing redistributed back-markers to produce an atypical late flourish.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires hold-up horses to race in their natural position rather than the compressed midfield they are likely to occupy, making it structurally unlikely given the redistribution of Big Apple Jack, White Umbrella, Impressor and others; White Umbrella's single soft-going win gives her the best profile if conditions somehow create the right shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Iris Dancer's position from stalls — if she breaks cleanly and immediately sets her own rhythm unchallenged, her uncontested lead on soft ground becomes a significant danger as no other runner has the profile or intent to press her.

Monitor Edgewater Drive's early movement from stall draw — returning from 298 days off, any sign of greenness or reluctance in the first furlong could see the prominent position lost entirely, changing the dynamic for the lead-tracking scenario.

White Umbrella and Big Apple Jack are genuine hold-up horses who will be racing out of role in midfield — watch whether Paul Mulrennan and Billy Garritty attempt to drop them out anyway, which would signal they expect a strong pace and are playing a late-race card rather than conforming to the compressed map.

The soft going is confirmed for this 6f trip and is identical to the race directly preceding it on the card — watch the winning time of the 4:50 5f to calibrate how testing the surface is, as an unusually slow time would further advantage front-runners who are not being pressed.

Doon The Glen and Summerstorms Dream represent the same Jim Goldie yard with a 3/29 14-day strike rate — if either is ridden with unexpected urgency early, it may signal stable confidence in a particular horse over the other, which would affect how the midfield shapes up through the first two furlongs.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing Tv Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: Most interesting profile in the race — has won twice at 20f on soft (Goodwood) and twice at 13f/16f on good, and arrives 73 days fresh under Rowan Scott; genuine stayer who relishes a strong test of stamina in soft going, and although a natural hold-up horse he has the form to sustain a run if produced with a prominent position here.
runners_data.comment: Perseus Way won last time out and also took a race four starts back, showing a clear ability to find the winning thread, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid asset; the chief concern is a 73-day absence leaving him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft for Dianne Sayer and James Sullivan partners well here; hold-up mare who has placed in soft going and returns after 23 days in manageable fitness; proven at 1m2f-1m4f but this 1m5f trip on soft is a step up in stamina and worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Simply Ruby arrives here as the top-rated runner in the field, with a winning strike and a third in recent starts suggesting she retains ability, and experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour; that unplaced effort last time is the main worry.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's runner arrives 32 days fresh with Greg Fairley; a true hold-up horse by nature whose recent form reads 797908 with no soft-going win in last 15 comparable runs — held by the map in midfield but in reality will want to come very late, which in a race where the leader dictates every yard is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ouro Preto has been consistently beaten in recent outings, though he has run over today's trip before and returns after a 32-day break carrying 135 lb; our rating of 67 suggests a shade more ability than his mark implies, yet his form makes improvement hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old returns 16 days after a run and Paul Mulrennan takes the ride; recent form of 006655 tells a tale of consistency without victory and the horse's natural inclination to race at the back of the field means it sits out of its preferred role here, carrying a Style_Fit penalty that tempers expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Spanish Hustle at least returns quickly on familiar distance and going, and our rating suggests he holds more ability than his official mark implies; consecutive fifths give faint encouragement, though a line through his form makes improvement hard to expect.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field — Bethell's three-year-old has won at 12f and 11f on good and shown pace; the concern is stepping from a win on good at 12f to soft at 1m5f, a significant test of stamina and ground adaptability, but the uncontested lead is a meaningful advantage.

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's three-year-old has placed twice on soft and is fitted with a hood; 25 days since last run and has run creditably at shorter trips, but the step to 1m5f on soft is the key stamina test and his recent 11th and 6th placings in soft conditions don't inspire confidence — Clifford Lee will need to produce a big ride.
runners_data.comment: Ibn Altheeb showed real promise when finishing third three starts back, and our rating of 70 comfortably clears his official mark of 64, making him a live threat despite being winless in recent starts — the concern is a return to form after an unplaced run last time.

runners_data.name: Billy No Mates
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's ten-year-old veteran returns after 75 days, a notable layoff for a horse of this age; won at 12f-15f on soft ground previously which is encouraging, and Connor Beasley is an able partner — but races as a natural hold-up horse who in this field will be unable to get close enough to the leader soon enough, softening his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 75 days off, Billy No Mates does have experience of today's distance and going in his favour, though a seventh last time out and a rating of 56 suggest he faces a stiff task picking up from midfield.

runners_data.name: Kindly Queen
runners_data.note: Christopher Kellett's three-year-old wears a hood and has placed three times in her last five starts including second on good; naturally prominent in style, she has a legitimate chance of tracking Clocker and benefiting if the pace eases — a soft-ground placing (5th at 12f) gives mild encouragement but this trip is new territory.
runners_data.comment: Kindly Queen has shown she can hit the frame, with a third two starts back and a second four starts back, but that ninth last time out is a concern after 39 days away, and she remains yet to win in recent starts despite carrying a workable 127 lb with experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Path To Peace
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's three-year-old is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and wears a visor; form of 9060 over shorter trips on varying ground offers nothing to enthuse about, and the stamina demands of 1m5f soft look likely to expose that weakness further — Shane Gray faces a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Path To Peace faces a stiff ask here; experience over today's trip and going is a modest positive, though her recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to raise enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Wootton's Gal
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's three-year-old has run second over 11f on good and has placed at 12f; Billy Garritty takes over and the mare's natural hold-up style means she'll be racing from deep in the pack — her soft-going experience is limited and the redistribution to midfield on the map doesn't reflect where she's likely to end up physically in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Wootton's Gal faces a stiff ask here, though a second three starts back and experience over today's trip offer slim encouragement after 32 days off carrying 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans's nine-year-old is fitted with a tongue strap and blinkers and Kevin Stott knows him well; won at 13f on good and placed at 15f on soft, giving him a credible staying profile — naturally prominent, he is one of only two horses in this field likely to track Clocker with genuine intent and is better positioned than his OR of 54 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Ebony Maw is hard to fancy at these weights, yet he does arrive with a win two starts back and has run over today's trip and going before, offering some small crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has three soft-ground placings from 15 comparable runs but no win in that condition; Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps with the 123lbs burden and the horse has finished 3rd-3rd-4th in its last three runs, suggesting consistent mid-division efforts — a true hold-up operator who won't get close enough to Clocker in this shape to threaten at the death.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Aighear is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 48-day break with a touch more scope on her speed rating than her official mark suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Clocker is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Oisin Orr in the plate for Edward Bethell, is likely to stride on from flag to finish over this 1m5f trip on soft ground at Hamilton, setting a genuine but controllable gallop rather than a suicidal one — there is no rival willing or able to chase him hard from the front. The field behind him is dominated by hold-up types, meaning the race will string out early with Clocker holding an unchallenged lead and the bulk of the field — Perseus Way, Simply Ruby, Ibn Altheeb, Billy No Mates, Wootton's Gal, Ouro Preto, Spanish Hustle and Aighear — all settled in the chasing pack. The soft ground at Hamilton will tax stayers and reward those with genuine stamina and the ability to close over a true test of distance, which on a sustained gallop set by one horse suits prominent and hold-up horses with proven soft-ground form making their move from two furlongs out. This race shape — a lone leader setting a steady, pressureless pace — most favours hold-up horses with confirmed soft-going credentials who can unleash a sustained run rather than a sharp kick, particularly those already proven at 1m5f or further; the field holds more true hold-up types than the pace map can show at the rear, and Ouro Preto, Wootton's Gal, Spanish Hustle, Billy No Mates and Aighear are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map but unlikely to secure a more forward position in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clocker Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker is allowed to bowl along in front without any rival forcing him to quicken, dictating a sustainable soft-ground gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Clocker sets his own fractions on soft ground and his rivals, all settled in a patient hold-up pack, face the dual challenge of making ground on a rested leader over the final 2f — those with a strong sustained finish rather than a sharp kick will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground takes a significant toll on Clocker in the final quarter-mile and the hold-up pack, tracking at a comfortable distance, find enough to reel him in.
scenarios.body: The leaders' advantage evaporates in the testing conditions as the genuine stayers among the hold-up group — particularly those with confirmed soft-ground wins — produce strong sustained finishes through the stamina-sapping closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Kindly Queen or Ebony Maw manage to track Clocker closely from the front and use their prominent style to pounce before the true hold-up horses can get to them.
scenarios.body: A closer pace gap between the leader and the prominent pack means Kindly Queen and Ebony Maw hit the straight with momentum and enough energy reserves to match or overhaul Clocker before the deep closers arrive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the ground proves significantly more testing than the going description suggests and the pace collapses, turning the race into a stop-start slog from halfway.
scenarios.body: An uneven tempo at a crawl followed by a desperate dash in heavy conditions turns the finish into a scramble where weight, freshness and course fitness matter most, benefiting lightly-weighted or recently-sharpened runners.

watchPoints.text: Clocker (Edward Bethell/Oisin Orr) is stepping from 12f on good to 1m5f on soft for the first time — if his stamina gives way in the final furlong the entire race shape collapses, making it critical to monitor whether he begins to idle or roll after the 2f pole.

Perseus Way arrives 73 days fresh and carries 142lbs — Rowan Scott will need to time the run perfectly from a hold-up position, as any traffic trouble in the closing stages at Hamilton could cost a horse whose form at 1m5f-2m on soft is the class benchmark in this field.

The weight of redistributed hold-up horses — Ouro Preto, Spanish Hustle, Wootton's Gal, Billy No Mates and Aighear — all racing out of their natural deep-closing role means the closing stages could become congested if Clocker slows, creating significant positional risks for backers of those horses.

Kindly Queen and Ebony Maw are the only two legitimate prominent-style horses capable of tracking Clocker into the straight — watch their positions at the 4f mark, as their ability to maintain contact with the leader into the final quarter-mile is the key swing factor in Scenarios A and C.

Soft ground at Hamilton has been confirmed throughout the card — any further deterioration in the going between the earlier races and the 5:50 slot could shift the balance further toward proven soft-ground performers and against horses whose best form is on good or faster.

races.name: Molton Brown Luxury Fragrance Hamilton Park 2-y-o Series Final Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Battle Fever
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott has a strong record aboard this Kevin Ryan-trained type who has hit the frame in all four career starts including a recent soft-ground second at Hamilton over this exact trip, giving him the most relevant course-and-conditions profile in the field.
runners_data.comment: Battle Fever shaped with real promise when second last time out, and a winner two starts back, he arrives here fresh on 13 days' rest, carrying 135 lb from stall one having already tackled today's trip; our rating of 97 marks him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Harley
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on this consistent Edward Bethell runner who has finished in the first three on five of six starts, all on good ground, making the step up to soft a notable question mark despite solid overall form.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner carries a tongue tie and has generally raced as a hold-up horse, though with so many closers in this field the gelding is likely to end up racing more prominently than ideal; recent form showing a 15th and 12th weakens confidence regardless of positioning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Rbflying does at least bring distance experience and a degree of freshness after just 13 days, though recent unplaced efforts and a ranking of sixth of eight on ratings suggest he faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 116 lb.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's colt has placed three times at 5f on good ground and looks progressive on that surface, but racing at 6f on soft represents twin steps into the unknown, and being pushed forward out of his natural closing role reduces the chance of producing his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Onslaught does bring two thirds from his recent outings to offset that, and has run over today's trip before; carrying 114 lb from stall eight, he sits in mid-division on our ratings and appeals as a competitive but not dominant player here.

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner under Finlay Bassett for Adrian Keatley, who has had no winners in the past 14 days; she has finished no better than fourth in four runs including a sixth on soft, but her uncontested lead is a genuine tactical asset regardless of raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Boutblummintime catches the eye with our rating putting him well clear of his official mark, and he has run over today's trip before, making him a genuine threat from stall five; the concern is that he has been winless in his last four starts, and that sequence of fourths and sixths will need reversing here.

runners_data.name: Trumpety Trump
runners_data.note: Lauren Young's claiming allowance is useful on a horse whose best recent effort — a second over 8f on soft — suggests she handles conditions well and stays, though dropping back to 6f from that winning trip is a question; this is the most interesting soft-ground profile among the hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Trumpety Trump faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and a return to form 12 days ago at least suggests he arrives fit.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner carries both blinkers and a tongue tie, has run just six days ago, and the form tab shows a pattern of fading finishes, with the ⚠ fade flag a serious concern on energy-sapping soft ground at a course that tests stamina.
runners_data.comment: Wild Terrain won five starts back and has run over today's trip, so the experience and proven ability to find the line are both there; the worry is his last four runs have shown that winning form hard to recapture, with a seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Sea Mirage
runners_data.note: The second Kevin Ryan runner in the race, ridden by a 5lb claimer, has placed at 6f on good ground twice recently and will naturally seek a prominent berth; soft ground represents a step into the unknown given all placed efforts have come on faster surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Sea Mirage is hard to fancy despite a return to a familiar trip; his latest outing did yield a second, though the wider recent profile — featuring two sixths — makes it difficult to build a case.

races.paceDynamic: Boutblummintime is the sole confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no credible challenger for the lead, meaning she can dictate a controlled tempo from the outset on soft ground over 6f at Hamilton. Battle Fever and Harley will press forward into prominent positions just off the leader, while Sea Mirage is also a natural prominent type who will seek to track close, creating a compact early order rather than a burning gallop. On soft ground with one leader setting a sustainable pace, the race is unlikely to be run at a true test of stamina, but the ground will nonetheless sap energy from front-runners who overextend, meaning horses travelling smoothly just off the pace are best placed to pounce. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the mapping can place at the rear — Rbflying and Onslaught are true closers who will likely find themselves racing closer than ideal given the prominent runners filling the early order. This race shape strongly favours prominent-position horses who can settle smoothly behind a controlled leader and produce a sustained finishing effort, rather than those needing a fast pace to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Boutblummintime dictates a comfortable, unchallenged tempo and prominent trackers conserve energy for a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Boutblummintime sets a manageable pace on soft ground, allowing Battle Fever and Harley to travel just behind her in a rhythm before unleashing their finish from 2f out; soft ground rewards those who have been covered up slightly rather than those who have expended energy fighting for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground creates a stamina grind and the pace slows dramatically in the final furlong, catching out lighter-weighted or tiring types.
scenarios.body: Boutblummintime's front-running slows to a crawl in the conditions, turning the race into an endurance test in the closing stages; horses with proven soft-ground form and the ability to sustain effort — namely Trumpety Trump and Harley — are best equipped to grind it out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run and a true closer manages to weave through.
scenarios.body: Rbflying or Onslaught finds the race run at a sufficient tempo that their natural hold-up style can be deployed, closing ground through tiring rivals in the final furlong; however, given both are mapped out of their natural role and the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, this remains the least structurally favoured outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate and the field so bunched that Boutblummintime simply steals an unassailable lead that rivals cannot close.
scenarios.body: On very soft ground with a deeply modest gallop, Boutblummintime's rivals fail to quicken adequately when it matters, leaving her just enough margin to hold on; her OR of 61 makes this a low-probability outcome but the scenario is live if the field is completely flat in the stretch.

watchPoints.text: Battle Fever is the only runner with a proven course win at this exact 6f Hamilton trip on soft going — watch if Kevin Stott positions him just off Boutblummintime's shoulder, as that combination of tactical placement and conditions form makes him the most dangerous horse in the field.

Boutblummintime is the sole front-runner and completely uncontested for the lead — if Finlay Bassett allows her to coast at an abnormally slow early pace, the race may become a procession that leaves challengers with too little to chase.

Wild Terrain has run within the last six days, carries headgear, and has a documented tendency to fade — on soft ground at Hamilton, any energy deficit from the quick turnaround could be brutally exposed in the final furlong.

Trumpety Trump's soft-ground second over 8f is an eye-catching stamina indicator — watch whether Lauren Young attempts to get her closer to the pace than expected, given the field's compressed midfield is likely to create traffic for genuine hold-up types.

Rbflying and Onslaught are both natural hold-up horses likely to find themselves racing in a position that does not suit their style — watch whether they manage to slot into a genuine closing position or whether the compressed field forces them to race more prominently than ideal.

races.name: Follow Us On X @hamiltonparkrc Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Call Me Betty
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up filly with soft-going form (won 6f soft last outing, sim-going 1W2P) and a good record over this trip for Michael Dods; Connor Beasley takes the ride after 86 days off, and her best chance depends on a strong pace to close into — rare in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Call Me Betty won two starts back but was well beaten last time out, and 86 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 140 lb is no featherweight, though a rating of 75 leaves room to compete here.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: David Allan partners this hold-up type who has done all her recent racing on good ground (0W0P in similar going), making the step to soft a significant concern; with no wins from 15 similar-going runs, she faces an uphill task regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner six starts back, Mae Amor has experience of today's trip and going and shaped with promise on her latest outing; carrying 140 lb from stall one, she rates the one to beat on an 84 rating, though the recent sequence demands some faith.

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly has placed four times at 6-7f on good ground and is not short of form, but has no soft-ground history on record; Clifford Lee rides and she is naturally a hold-up type, so she needs a strong pace she is unlikely to get here.
runners_data.comment: Diamont Katie shaped with real promise when second two starts back, and her speed rating of 80 gives her strong claims at the weights carrying 139 lb from stall ten; the main concern is her unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4-year-old has placed on both good and soft-ish surfaces and brings course-relevant form, but is a true rear-of-field horse whose natural position is at the back — pushed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding, so her real tactical challenge is finding a run from further back than shown.

runners_data.name: Kilfrush Desert
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3-year-old filly has consistent form at 5-6f on good and standard, placing twice at 6f on good ground; soft is untested, but Kevin Stott knows how to position a horse, and the natural hold-up style is compromised by a race shape that is unlikely to generate the gallop she needs.
runners_data.comment: Kilfrush Desert has finished second twice and third once in her last four starts, showing consistent placed form, and has run over today's trip; carrying 131 lb from stall nine, the main risk is whether she can convert that reliability into a winning run after a winless recent spell.

runners_data.name: Annie Edson Taylor
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground (6f GOO) and wears a tp (tongue-tie/pull) for Phillip Makin; her soft-going sim record reads 1W3P from 15 runs, and while she has the ability, her true hold-up style — forced into a midfield berth by runner congestion — leaves her reliant on a pace scenario that looks unlikely to materialise.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and beaten in her last two starts, Annie Edson Taylor faces a stiff task, though she does bring distance and going experience to the table and a winning return to form three starts back hints at ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's 3-year-old was placed twice at 6f on good ground and ran just 12 days ago, so fitness is not the question; having raced over 6f soft before (6th), she has surface exposure, but as a natural closer, the modest expected tempo in this race gives her slim realistic hope of overhauling the leader.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Whiskey Kisses faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive fit on a 12-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going before, and her second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lily Pearl
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the field for Richard & Fahey; won over 6f soft before (1W1P similar going) and, returning after 90 days off, Ethan Tindall (claim) takes over — her ability to boss an uncontested lead on testing ground is the defining tactical factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Lily Pearl won three starts back and was third two starts back, showing she retains the ability to compete at this level, and our rating of 79 supports her claims; the main concern is a 90-day absence heading into this.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 5-year-old won over 6f on good recently (form: 226291) and is among those most likely to push forward from her redistributed midfield position, racing closer to the pace than her hold-up label suggests; soft ground is unexplored in her recent history, and Lauren Young (5lb claim) adds a cost-saving angle.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Thunderstorm Katie faces a stiff ask, yet she does bring a recent win and a placed effort in her last six starts, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 25 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4-year-old has an excellent record with multiple wins and places at 6f, though all recent form is on good ground (0W0P in similar going); as one of the more capable horses in the field, Jack Nicholls (3lb claim) partners her, and she is among those who may press forward to challenge Lily Pearl — though soft going remains an open question.
runners_data.comment: Invincible Ruby showed her quality with a win three starts back, though she was only ninth last time out and that dip in form is the concern; she has run over today's trip and returns after 26 days, but consistency is the question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Lily Pearl is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner field and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge her, she should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset on soft ground at Hamilton. The absence of any rival willing or able to pressure her early means the tempo is entirely under her control — she can dictate a sustainable gallop that flatters her stamina and makes it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel her in over just six furlongs. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types, and the race shape strongly favours Lily Pearl and any horse capable of travelling prominently close to her, as the likely moderate early fractions on soft ground will compress the finish and leave closers with insufficient time or ground to close. Several runners — including Thunderstorm Katie, Kilfrush Desert, Invincible Ruby, Pickersgill, Annie Edson Taylor, and Whiskey Kisses — are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of these, Thunderstorm Katie and Invincible Ruby are most likely to push forward and secure a position closer to the pace than their natural style would suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lily Pearl Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lily Pearl bowls clear from the gate and faces no early pressure, controlling tempo throughout on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Lily Pearl sets a measured but race-winning gallop, building a lead that soft ground and six furlongs make very hard to peg back for hold-up horses with nowhere near enough time to close; the front-runner's profile is the standout beneficiary of a lone-pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or two redistributed runners push forward early and race close to Lily Pearl, filling the prominent slots and dominating the finish.
scenarios.body: A small group settles just off the pace and reaches the final furlong with reserves intact, while true hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by the moderate tempo; runners who punch forward from their mapped midfield positions gain a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Lily Pearl's uncontested lead proves illusory and the early pace is fast enough on soft ground to cause her to weaken inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The front-runner ties up on the testing surface, leaving a small gap for hold-up horses with genuine soft-ground form to pick up late; however, this scenario depends heavily on horses racing out of their redistributed roles, which materially limits its likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground causes the early pace to be so slow that the field bunches and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A slow-motion contest turns into a dash for home where tactical acuity and a sharp finishing kick matter more than position or style; horses with a clean passage and ability to quicken on soft ground benefit, though few in this field have convincingly demonstrated that combination.

watchPoints.text: Lily Pearl's uncontested lead is the single biggest danger signal in this race — if she gets clear and unchallenged in the first furlong on soft ground, hold-up horses are almost certainly racing for the minor places.

Thunderstorm Katie and Invincible Ruby are the two redistributed hold-up types most likely to push forward and occupy the prominent slots — watch their early positions at the break, as this will determine whether Scenario A or B dominates.
Mae Amor's 0-from-15 record on similar going is a stark flag against her chances regardless of race shape; if punters are backing her, the soft ground stats suggest significant risk.

The majority of this field — six or more runners — have done their best recent work on good or faster ground, and the universal soft going today at Hamilton could compress the form significantly, making soft-going experience (Call Me Betty, Lily Pearl, Whiskey Kisses) a key differentiator.

Lily Pearl's 90-day absence and the use of a 5lb apprentice jockey (Ethan Tindall) are the two variables most likely to undermine the dominant scenario — if she is ring-rusty or ridden conservatively, the race shape changes materially.

races.name: #cleanstay At Hampton By Hilton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Soft-going form is solid (2nd at 10f in Soft last outing), stays this trip well, and Jack Nicholls taking the 3lb claim is a useful allowance boost; a genuine hold-up horse who will be dropping in from the rear but has the ground form to make that count.
runners_data.comment: Tee Aitch Aye arrives here in sound form, placing second last time out and third two starts back, and 23 days between runs leaves him fresh for this test; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a mark of 60 looks workable for a gelding yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr runner whose best form has come on Good ground (two wins over 8f on Good), and the shift to Soft over a longer 12½f trip looks a significant ask; all five recent runs on Good suggest this going change is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Palmarian arrives on the back of a second three starts back and a win four starts back, showing he knows how to perform when in the mood; he has run over today's trip and returns after 19 days, but his two most recent efforts — a fourth and an eighth — are the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the Easterbys who can slot in behind Kelpie Grey, though a string of five-place finishes without a win in recent form and a tendency to run in Good-ground sprints raises doubts about his effectiveness on Soft over this extended trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Keats House nonetheless rates a clear 10 lb above his official mark on our figures — the strongest reading in the field — and he has distance and going experience to call on; the risk is that his recent finishing positions offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: The sole front runner in the race — a 6yo for Jim Goldie who is running out of his usual shorter-distance comfort zone, with his last five runs all at 6-7f on Soft or Good; the STYLE_FIT flag acknowledges this is a trip and role stretch, but he sets the entire tactical shape regardless.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of ten on ratings and clocking a speed figure of 73, Kelpie Grey brings experience over today's trip and conditions, and 23 days between runs leaves him fresh enough to strike; the concern is a winless recent spell that includes several unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Jim Goldie mapped to midfield due to the surplus of closers in this field; has placed form on Soft over 10f and handles the going, though racing outside her most comfortable position is a mild disadvantage on a day when getting cover matters.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Penelope's Sister faces a stiff task here, though the third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran also trained by Goldie, truly a hold-up horse shifted to the midfield section because of the crowded rear; recent form has been solid (three 3rd-place finishes in last five) but entirely at shorter trips of 7-8f, and the 12½f trip here looks a significant stamina test.
runners_data.comment: Yaaser arrives 23 days fresh after a fourth last time out, and consecutive thirds three and four starts back show he can hit the frame, yet he remains winless in recent starts and his draw from stall 10 is worth noting heading into this.

runners_data.name: Mimi's Magic
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on Ed Dunlop's 3yo filly, who showed her best form with a 2nd over 10f at Sandown (Standard); last run was a disappointing 9th and all her form is on artificial or Good ground, so the Soft is an unknown quantity worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with her recent finishes trending the wrong way, Mimi's Magic faces an uphill task from stall nine off 132 lb, though she has run over today's trip before and a second and third in earlier efforts show she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Fahey 3yo filly who has placed twice on Soft (3rd and 6th) and handles soft ground reasonably, though all five career runs have been at shorter trips; her true hold-up style is displaced into a midfield berth here, and Oisin Orr will need to manage traffic carefully on a debut over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Aurelune is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip before and stall one is hers to utilise; the third last time offers a crumb of comfort, but 60 days off the track adds to the concern.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: A 3yo for Adrian Nicholls whose form is thin — a 4th on Good at 8f is the best showing — and his one soft-ground run produced a 10th; blinkered and with a STYLE_FIT flag, this genuinely hold-up horse bumping around in a crowded midfield on soft ground over 12½f looks difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a seventh last time out and little else to encourage from recent efforts, Scheffler faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip before and 30 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, but that is about as far as the case goes.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's 4yo carries the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag, which is a clear concern in a soft-ground stamina test; a genuine closer mapped to midfield, he has shown ability to place at shorter trips (2nd twice recently) but the combination of soft ground and 12½f is a worrying profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Toy Soldier has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet his recent string of sixth, seventh and eighth placings make improvement essential; 130 lb from stall three is the ask, though earlier placed efforts hint at residual ability.

races.paceDynamic: Kelpie Grey is the sole confirmed front runner in this 10-runner soft-ground mile-and-a-half contest at Hamilton, and with no other horse likely to seriously dispute the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, uncontested tempo from the outset. On soft ground over this trip, even a moderate gallop will test stamina, and a horse bowling along in front without pressure can dictate exactly how hard the race is run — likely setting a sustainable but not dawdling pace that stretches the field on the collar uphill. That dynamic favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the pace in midfield and produce a measured finish rather than a flat-out sprint, making the race shape most hospitable to prominent racers and genuine midfield closers who handle this ground. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can honestly accommodate at the rear: Penelope's Sister, Yaaser, Aurelune, Scheffler, and Toy Soldier are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield slots, meaning several will be racing uncomfortably wide or in a bunched group, and of the pure closers, Tee Aitch Aye and Mimi's Magic are best placed to secure a genuine tracking position without being squeezed out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kelpie Grey Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey leads uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate soft-ground gallop that gradually wears the field down.
scenarios.body: Kelpie Grey dictates every yard on her own terms, and the steady pace on soft ground stretches stamina without triggering a dramatic late cavalry charge; runners who travel smoothly in her slipstream are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Kelpie Grey at close range throughout and produces a well-timed challenge from second or third entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The controlled pace means no dramatic injection of speed is needed — a horse positioned just behind the leader throughout simply picks Kelpie Grey off in the final furlong without needing a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey sets a genuinely strong enough pace on the soft ground to bring true hold-up horses into play with a late run.
scenarios.body: A punishing tempo drains the leaders and allows runners who settle midfield to pick up the pieces in the closing stages; Tee Aitch Aye has soft-ground form and experience coming from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the going proves particularly testing and the race becomes a battle of stamina rather than any specific tactical shape.
scenarios.body: Runners who have demonstrated stamina on soft or heavy ground and whose trainers have targeted this trip specifically come to the fore; most of the hold-up types are disadvantaged if their redistribution means they race without cover.

watchPoints.text: Kelpie Grey controls the tempo unchallenged — if Paul Mulrennan is allowed to bowl along in front without any pressure, he will set the race's entire rhythm and runners unable to track him closely on soft ground may find themselves with too much to do.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Penelope's Sister, Yaaser, Aurelune, Scheffler, Toy Soldier) will likely be racing bunched in a group, creating traffic risk turning into the straight — watch for interference or horses failing to find gaps at a critical point.

Palmarian's going suitability is questionable — all recent form is on Good ground at shorter trips, and if the Soft proves genuinely testing, James Sullivan may find him struggling to land a blow from his hold-up position.

Toy Soldier carries the fades-in-finish note — in a soft-ground 12½f handicap where stamina is at a premium, backers should note he has a habit of emptying late, which could make him a false lead candidate if he tracks the pace rather than sitting off it.

Three Jim Goldie runners (Kelpie Grey, Penelope's Sister, Yaaser) sharing the same T14 record of 3/29 — stable in decent form, and with one setting the pace and two closers behind, there is a potential stable tactical play worth monitoring during running.

races.name: Book Your Christmas Party Hamilton Park Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Jim Goldie with a recent win 6 days ago over 11f on good; steps up to soft ground today which appears within range, and Paul Mulrennan provides a strong booking — watch for a prominent move from the rear group.
runners_data.comment: Annandale ran a cracker last time, finishing second six days ago, and has run over today's trip and going — he maps as a lively threat from stall five carrying 135 lb, though the quick turnaround is the one question connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose sole soft-ground record (5/15, 0W1P) suggests caution on this surface, though a recent win and three placings show current form; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim could compensate for any going concern.
runners_data.comment: Sophiesticate arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here; the main risk is whether 134 lb proves too stiff a burden at this level.

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Holds genuine hold-up form including a soft-ground placing, but the map has pushed this horse into a midfield position it is unlikely to naturally occupy — its true style needs a strong gallop to deliver, which this shape is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Dubai Venture has been in fine form, finishing second last time out and second two starts back, with a win three starts back, and he handles today's trip and going; the concern is that 134 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Vampire Slayer
runners_data.note: Extensive soft-ground and heavy-ground form (12/15 runs, 2 wins) makes this the standout going qualifier; the 166-day absence is a concern but Shane Gray rides and the horse has proven stamina over 16-18f, though today's 1m3f is shorter than its optimum.
runners_data.comment: Vampire Slayer has shown he can mix it at this level, finishing second two starts back and a second four starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; winless in his last five, and 166 days off the track, but a rating of 68 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Hickton
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on standard recently but the soft-ground record is limited; a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping role it may not occupy naturally, and the style-fit discount applies given this race's moderate tempo.
runners_data.comment: Hickton has managed just one win in his last six starts, finishing fifth last time out and no better than sixth in the two runs prior, so it is hard to make a case for him against stronger-rated rivals, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround in reasonable nick.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on good but all five recent runs came on good ground and the soft-going record is thin; a genuine hold-up horse that Daniel Tudhope picks up for Goldie, though 59 days off and an out-of-role redistribution temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Uncle Liam won three starts back but has posted a pair of mid-division finishes since, and 59 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 58 offers a small edge over his official mark.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and should secure uncontested lead from the off; visor retained, ran 6 days ago, and Katie Scott's yard has a quiet 14-day record — soft ground is unexplored territory but controlling the pace is its biggest asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Falaise Blanc finished fourth last time out just six days ago and, ranked eighth of nine on our figures, is hard to fancy at the weights despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has failed to recapture earlier form, with recent efforts on good and soft both uninspiring; Connor Beasley takes the ride but the horse is a true hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution, and its recent form string offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Dandy's Angel is winless in her last five starts, though she posted a third three starts back to show she retains some ability; back quickly after just five days, she has experience over today's trip and going, but her rating of 47 gives her plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Goldie's third runner, a four-year-old with limited soft-ground form (0W0P in 2 runs) and a patchy recent record; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a small positive but this horse is another redistribution case whose natural position at the rear may prove difficult to exploit off a slow pace.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Spirit Of Nature faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip before and 22 days between runs suggests he is at least fit, but a mark of 47 and draw 1 offer little obvious leverage.

races.paceDynamic: Falaise Blanc is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and should lead from the outset over 1m3f on soft ground at Hamilton, setting a sustainable but unchallenged gallop that is unlikely to be pressured into anything reckless. With no other genuine pace horse to push the tempo, the fractions will almost certainly be controlled and even, giving Falaise Blanc every opportunity to conserve energy through the middle stages and kick again approaching the home straight. The bulk of the field — Annandale, Sophiesticate, Vampire Slayer, Dubai Venture, Hickton, Uncle Liam, Dandy's Angel, and Spirit Of Nature — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning the race will be run as a steady-tempo affair with a compressed, congested pack stalking the leader. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven soft-ground stamina who can deliver a sustained late run, rather than those who need a genuine end-to-end gallop to stretch their rivals — horses like Vampire Slayer and Annandale, both proven on soft, are best positioned to exploit this setup. Note also that Dubai Venture, Hickton, Uncle Liam, Dandy's Angel, and Spirit Of Nature are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because this field holds far more horses wanting to come from behind than the race shape can genuinely accommodate; Falaise Blanc is most likely to secure the lead, with Sophiesticate and Annandale the most plausible to latch onto prominent ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Falaise Blanc Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Falaise Blanc bowls along at a moderate, uncontested clip and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap efficiently on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Falaise Blanc controls every yard at a comfortable tempo, using the soft conditions to sap the energy of closers who must generate momentum from a plodding pace; the home straight sees the leader already into stride while the pack is still at full stretch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stayers Grind Home
scenarios.trigger: If the steady tempo sets up a stamina-based grind in the home straight and the truest soft-ground stayers produce a relentless late surge.
scenarios.body: Vampire Slayer's proven record in soft and heavy conditions over staying trips puts it in prime position, while Annandale's consistent form on good ground gives it claims if the softness is not as testing as feared; both can deliver sustained efforts rather than sudden acceleration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses travelling prominently behind the leader get a better trip than the wider hold-up pack and land a decisive blow in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sophiesticate, capable of racing prominently, would benefit from a clean passage tracking the pace and quickening off a slow tempo; Annandale, with a recent win and course knowledge, could also exploit a well-judged prominent position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group gets into each other's way and the redistributed horses — racing out of their natural roles — fail to produce genuine late runs.
scenarios.body: Dubai Venture and Hickton, both mapped out of their true hold-up roles and carrying style-fit discounts, would struggle most in this shape as the modest pace never generates the strong gallop they need; this scenario produces a muddling finish with few horses delivering their best.

watchPoints.text: Vampire Slayer's soft-ground credentials (12/15 career runs on soft or heavy, two wins) stand out in this field — watch whether Shane Gray angles this horse for a clear run into the straight, as it is the most proven stayer under these conditions.

Falaise Blanc sets the pace from stall draw — if the early tempo is genuinely slow, the entire hold-up pack risks being caught flat-footed on the testing ground when they try to quicken, turning this into a procession for the leader.

Daniel Tudhope riding Uncle Liam is a notable jockey booking for a Goldie runner, but the horse's redistribution out of its natural hold-up role and absence of soft-ground form means connections may find it difficult to get competitive at this trip and tempo.

Jim Goldie saddles three runners (Annandale, Uncle Liam, Spirit Of Nature) — watch whether Annandale, the most in-form of the trio with a recent win and consistent placed efforts, becomes the yard's main hope, potentially drawing tactical support from the others.

The combined soft-going record across the field is modest outside Vampire Slayer — if the going deteriorates further during the evening session, the gulf between proven soft-ground handlers and the rest could be more significant than market prices reflect.
